correctness.rationale: Every projection onto the codimension-one kernel has rank-one form a rank-one correction; the Daugavet rank-one identity gives the exact projection-norm identity. For a bounded L-Lipschitz g, the two-sided pair inequality g(t)−g(−t)≤2 min(||g||∞,Lt) is saturated pointwise by the clipped ramp, proving the exact budget and root uniqueness. Strictly positive density implies equality rigidity and unique correction. Subtracting its moment equation from normalization yields an exact near-zero tail integral, with dominated convergence establishing the exponent and coefficient. Power densities are integrated exactly, and the inverse curve follows algebraically. Standalone code executed 288 numerical assertions; no infinite claim rests on finite tests.

value.rationale: Determines the exact optimum under every feasible Lipschitz budget for an entire natural infinite-dimensional family of nonattaining hyperplane projection problems, classifies the unique optimizing correction, sharp critical budget, and sharp regularity cost, and identifies arbitrary decay exponents through the sign-change cusp. It explains quantitative distinctions invisible to the existing uniform hyperplane constant 2 and furnishes an exact inverse approximation budget, beyond a single finite calculation or parameter substitution.
